children: Ord Minnett isn't sweating Whitehaven Coal's lack of progress in bringing its debt down during the September quarter. Net debt rose to 1.4 billion Australian dollars, above Ord Minnett's A$1.2 billion expectation. That reflected port disruptions, which weighed on equity coal sales. Still, analyst Tim Elder was upbeat about Whitehaven's operational performance. Run-of-mine production of 11.0 million tons was impressive, with quarterly costs at the lower end of FY27 guidance. "While this result was not the start of deleveraging that we had hoped for, Whitehaven's strong operating performance gives us confidence that the balance sheet will improve over the coming quarters," Ord Minnett says. It forecasts A$1.0 billion of net debt by the end of June. Ord Minnett has a buy call on Whitehaven.(david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
